summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a sheet name.
description: `nonValidSheetName(value)` is the same test as `!isValidSheetName(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
What Google Sheets accepts: at most 100 characters, not blank, none of `\ / ? * [ ]`, and not the reserved name `history` in any case.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a sheet name; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonValidSheetName("history"); // => true
nonValidSheetName("Data/2026"); // => true
nonValidSheetName(""); // => true
nonValidSheetName("Data"); // => false
nonValidSheetName("Report 2026"); // => false
```
